deep.reconstruction:
Notation (fixed by the neighbouring pages and confirmed numerically). For weight w = m+n = 13, q^s denotes Euler's sum Σ_x x^{-s} Σ_{y≤x} y^{-(13-s)}, which equals ζ(s,13-s)+ζ(13) in modern double-zeta notation (n>m). p^13 denotes ζ(13). Inside each row, p^k (k=2..6) is shorthand for the product ζ(k)ζ(13-k); an asterisk means coefficient 0.

What the page does. Euler writes the conjectured reduction of all q^s (s=12,...,2) to ζ(13) and the five products. Three kinds of entries appear:
(1) The p^2...p^5 columns, extrapolated from weights 5, 7, 9 and 11. The visible pattern is C(11,k) in the p^2 column and C(8,k)-type sums in the p^4 column.
(2) The ζ(13) coefficients A...L, generated by the recursion A=(w+1)/2 and k·X_k=(w+1-k)·X_{k-1} ± (w+1)/2 with alternating sign. This gives 7, 77/2, 287/2, 357, 644, 1715/2, 1717/2, 643, 358, 285/2, 79/2.
(3) A new column p^6=ζ(6)ζ(7) with unknowns β...λ. The reflection identity q^s+q^{13-s}=ζ(s)ζ(13-s)+ζ(13) forces λ=β, κ=γ, ι=δ, θ=ε and η=ζ-1. Euler then guesses ('videturque esse') β=6, γ=15, δ=20, ε=15, ζ=6+1, i.e. binomial coefficients C(6,k).

§33 begins rewriting each odd order in a uniform layout to make the general law visible and remove the 'anomalies' (the extra +1's and the split coefficients such as 56+1, 70+8).

Modern check.
- The recursion is equivalent to the closed form X_k = [C(w,k) + (-1)^{k+1}]/2. So the coefficient of ζ(w) in ζ(s,t) is ½[(-1)^s C(w,s) - 1].
- The full table agrees with the Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) odd-weight formula. Each ζ(2j)ζ(w-2j) gets (-1)^t[C(w-2j-1,s-1)+C(w-2j-1,t-1)], plus ½(1+(-1)^s)ζ(s)ζ(t), plus the ζ(0)=-1/2 term giving ζ(w).
- I verified every entry of the p^2, p^3 and p^6 columns and all eleven ζ(13) coefficients, e.g. q^11: 6=C(6,1); q^7: C(6,6)+C(6,5)=7; q^6: -7+1=-6.
- Sanity check: q^12 gives Σ H_n/n^12 = 7ζ(13) - Σ_{k=2}^{6} ζ(k)ζ(13-k), which is the classical formula.

What the page serves: the inductive discovery of the general evaluation of linear Euler sums / double zeta values of odd weight.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All guessed values β..λ and the ζ(13) coefficients A..L are correct by the modern (BBG 1995) formula.
The p^6 column is explicitly conjectural ('videturque esse'), not derived on this page.
In the q^12 row the sign before p^5 is badly printed (looks like '÷'). It must be '−' (q^12 = 7p^13 − p^2 − p^3 − p^4 − p^5 − p^6).

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known inductive part of E477 leading to Euler's odd-weight theorem for double zeta values, which is widely credited to Euler (e.g. by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn). All entries check out, and no new or unexploited idea appears here.
